A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAR3D, with the same central method and experiments. All 16 pages of each version are readable, including equations, figures, tables, and the relocated supplementary material.

before.justification: V1 reports original quantitative image-to-3D results in Table 1 and qualitative generation and captioning results in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V3 retains the original generation and captioning experiments, updates Table 1, and adds VQVAE reconstruction results in supplementary Figure S1.

M1.justification: The multi-scale VQVAE, autoregressive generation, losses, and truncated-token captioning procedure remain unchanged. V3 explicitly describes two-stage LLM finetuning in Section 4.3, but v1 already references that procedure in Section 3.2 and reports both training stages.

E1.justification: Both versions use G-Objaverse objects and 3DTopia captions for the same generation and captioning tasks. The added reconstruction examples examine the existing VQVAE reconstruction task; they do not establish a new dataset, domain, or distinct test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same eight image-to-3D baselines, including unchanged comparator subsets in Figures 4 and S3. Figure 6 retains Point-E, Shap-E, 3DTopia, and LN3Diff. The new training-data table documents existing comparators.

E3.justification: Reported resolutions, model configurations, batch sizes, metrics, and latency procedures remain unchanged. However, v3 retains approximately 176K training objects in Section 5 while newly listing 170K for SAR3D in Table S1. Whether this reflects coarse reporting or a changed training subset is unresolved.

E4.justification: V3 adds a qualitative reconstruction study in supplementary Section A and Figure S1, comparing ground truth and reconstructions for objects with holes, complex geometry, and textures. Existing supplementary generation and captioning examples are retained; no component ablation is added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new Table S1 gives training-data quantities rather than statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises SAR3D-NeRF MUSIQ/COV/MMD from 67.24/71.50/15.24 to 65.77/74.17/13.63, and Flexicubes from 65.17/59.50/15.48 to 67.24/71.50/15.25. Flexicubes consequently has the highest MUSIQ. Baseline scores, FID, KID, and latency remain unchanged. Figure S1 adds reconstruction results; the numerical revisions are unexplained.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 and supplementary Algorithms 1–2 retain the same mathematical content. The added reconstruction explanation and scalability discussion introduce no formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: multi-scale autoregressive 3D generation, 0.82-second generation on an A6000, and detailed captioning using truncated 3D tokens, including simultaneous generation and captioning.

C2.justification: Section 6 replaces the assertion of inherent scalability with an explicit statement that scalability remains unverified, citing VAR's 2D scaling laws as suggestive evidence. New supplementary Section A attributes reconstruction fidelity to capturing global and local features. Other limitations and interpretations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: New Table S1 discloses training-data quantities for SAR3D and its baselines, and supplementary Section D explicitly states that pretrained baseline models were used. These are additional disclosures, rather than demonstrated changes to baseline training. Main implementation details and the project URL are retained.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds a limited argument connecting prospective SAR3D scalability to VAR's 2D scaling laws. The distinct cited works otherwise remain unchanged: the bibliography contracts from 95 to 92 entries by consolidating duplicate GPT-3, LRM, and latent-diffusion references, alongside metadata updates.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized clarifications and language edits, adds acknowledgements, moves references before the supplement, and reorders supplementary sections. The main narrative and section structure remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds reconstruction Figure S1 and training-data Table S1, refreshes overview illustrations, and adjusts figure placement and sizing. The former transformer Figure S1 becomes S2, and captioning Figure S2 becomes S4; their content is retained, as is comparison Figure S3.

improvement.justification: V3 adds targeted reconstruction evidence, clarifies baseline provenance and training-data quantities, and qualifies its scalability discussion more carefully. These modestly improve support and transparency. Unexplained Table 1 revisions and the unreconciled 170K versus approximately 176K training counts limit the gains; higher reported scores alone do not establish better paper quality.
